title: Cultural Exchange: Global Influence
description: Spread your cultural influence across regions of the world! Place cultural landmarks and traditions to win over territories held by a rival civilization. Learn about soft power, cultural diversity, and how ideas travel across borders through strategic placement.
learning_objectives: Understand how cultural exchange shapes societies and nations
Learn about soft power and its role in global influence
Explore the dynamics of cultural diversity and coexistence
Practice strategic thinking in spreading ideas across territories
Recognize how cultural influence can shift allegiances and viewpoints
Appreciate the interplay between tradition and innovation in global culture
how_to_play: Place your cultural influence disc on the board adjacent to the rival culture's territory.
Any rival culture discs caught in a straight line between your new disc and an existing one are converted to your culture.
You must convert at least one rival territory with each move — if you can't, your turn is skipped.
Corners represent deep-rooted cultural strongholds that can never be flipped once claimed.
The game ends when neither civilization can expand further.
The civilization with the most cultural influence on the board wins!

storybook_pages.title: A World of Cultures
storybook_pages.text: Two great civilizations meet at the crossroads of history. Each brings art, music, philosophy, and traditions that can win the hearts of people across the globe. Your mission: spread your cultural influence strategically, turning rival territories into allies through the power of ideas.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: world map with two colorful civilizations spreading across continents, cultural icons like masks, instruments, and temples on a game grid, vibrant purple and orange colors, cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: The Power of Soft Influence
storybook_pages.text: Unlike war, cultural exchange wins through attraction, not coercion. A well-placed festival can convert an entire region. A corner position — like founding a major university — creates an unshakeable cultural anchor. Think globally, act strategically.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: diverse cultural symbols — theater masks, musical notes, books, food, festivals — spreading across a grid board like ripples in water, colorful and educational, cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Legacy of Exchange
storybook_pages.text: As the board fills, the map of cultural influence tells a story. Regions that were once rivals now share traditions and ideas. The civilization with the broadest reach has shaped the world — but both sides have learned from each other in the process.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: completed game board showing a mosaic of two blended cultures, people from different backgrounds celebrating together, cultural landmarks scattered across the grid, warm celebratory cartoon style

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

achievements.name: Flip Master
achievements.description: Flipped 10+ opponent pieces in a single move

cultural_context: India's extraordinary cultural diversity — 1,600+ languages, dozens of religions, multiple classical traditions — makes cross-cultural understanding a core civic competency. This game develops the perspective-taking and empathy that enable students to navigate India's plural society.
reflection_prompt: Which flip changed the shape of the game most? What did you not see coming?
